The '''HP&nbsp;9g''' (F2222A) is a [[graphing calculator]] designed by [[Kinpo Electronics]], Inc and produced by [[Hewlett-Packard]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kinpo.com.tw/English/product_consumer_1.html |title=產品訊息 |publisher=Kinpo.com.tw |date= |access-date=2014-03-10}}</ref> It has basic graphing, scientific and [[computer programming|programming features]] designed for use by students.

Despite resembling a typical [[scientific calculator]] in appearance, such as those by competitors [[Casio]] and [[Sharp Corporation|Sharp]], the 9g departs from HP calculator tradition because it does not have an [[Reverse Polish Notation|RPN]] mode. It is also particular unusual for its display, which includes a compact [[Dot-matrix display|dot-matrix]] grid for displaying graphs, a dot-matrix character line which displays expressions being input (acting as a continuation of the dot-matrix grid), and a [[seven-segment display|seven-segment]] line to display answers to expressions.

The HP 9g is similar to Citizen SRP-325G, also designed by Kinpo Electronics, Inc.
